conviction_note: abs_move 3.5 (baseline median 3.18 on 7 prints, no option chain, ~$26k/day tape) times a p_up of 45: the one new-ish company number (brand partners stabilised at ~5,200, a -10% YoY comp after -31% and -58%) was said on 9 July and the stock still fell 3.2% on that print; the bottom line is unlikely to narrow against the year-ago $(1.29)m because the year-ago tax benefit and Hilti rental income are gone while interest expense is also gone, and six of seven prior reactions were negative. Findings net to -0.3, same sign as the scaled number, both small.
bar: No sell-side estimate exists (MarketBeat's $53.10m 'consensus' for Q1 FY27 against $4.76m actual is a data error, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-9-educational-development-co-stock/). The bar is the company's own year-ago quarter: Q2 FY26 net revenues $4,621,100 (PaperPie $3,731,200, Publishing $889,900), net loss $(1,294,700), EPS $(0.15), average active brand partners 5,800, from the 10-Q filed 2025-10-09 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/31667/000118518525001415/educ10q083125.htm. Because no consensus can be sourced, every size below is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 30.7K shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 23.2K (09-15) and 18.5K (08-31), about 0.4% of 8.52m shares outstanding, 1.0 days to cover (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/educ/short-interest/, settlement 2026-09-30). No squeeze mechanism and no crowded short. No option chain, so no skew; the baseline's only directional statement is the reaction history (1 up in 7, median |3.18%|). Tape: spot $1.315, +1.15% over 5 and 20 days, -20.3% from the 52-week high, +6.05% from the low, 19,592 shares/day average.

findings.finding: Active PaperPie brand partners stopped falling: 5,200 at end-May 2026 (up 20% from 4,300 at end-February) and, per the CEO on the 9 July call, 'stayed at that level' into July, against a year-ago Q2 FY26 average of 5,800; that is a roughly -10% YoY partner comp for the quarter ended 31 Aug 2026 after -31% in Q1 FY27 and -58% in Q2 FY26, the first quarter in eleven where the decline would be in single-to-low-double digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Partner count is the line the sweep names as operating; the stock fell 3.18% on 2026-07-09 when the 20% sequential rise was first disclosed, and 9.94% on 2025-10-09 when Q2 FY26 showed 5,800 vs 13,900. Six of seven baseline reactions negative.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 5,200 figure was public on 9 July and the stock is flat (+1.15%) over 20 days with no coverage and no estimate. If the market had priced a stabilised salesforce, the stock would not sit 20% off its high at $11m of market cap against $36m of inventory. What is new is whether the level held through August and what revenue per partner the summer produced; nobody has a number for that.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 release gives the 4,300 to 5,200 figures (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/304633/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Results, 2026-07-09); shares the transcript with the new-titles finding below.

findings.finding: The first full quarter of new titles since the lender-imposed purchasing freeze: the 10-Q says new-title purchases were restricted for the first three quarters of FY26, Usborne purchases were $0 in Q1 FY27, and management said on 9 July the major new-title release came in mid-June with 'strong early reception', so Q2 FY27 (Jun-Aug) is the first summer quarter with fresh product since 2024.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has carried a new-title cycle in this period; the 2025-07-07 print (-3.7%) and 2025-10-09 (-9.94%) were quarters with the freeze in force.
findings.why_not_priced: Revenue per active partner in Q2 FY26 was about $643 (PaperPie $3.73m / 5,800) in a quarter with no new product; if new titles lift that even 10% on 5,200 partners, PaperPie revenue is near the year-ago $3.73m despite fewer partners. No published number exists on this; management refused to give a new-title mix percentage on the call.
findings.independence: Transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15219109458093056, 2026-07-09) for the mid-June release timing; shares that document with the partner-count finding, which rests on a different fact.

findings.finding: Reported net loss is unlikely to narrow against the year-ago $(1,294,700) even though $603,200 of year-ago interest expense is gone: the year-ago quarter carried an income-tax benefit (25.8% effective rate in Q1 FY26) that no longer exists because a valuation allowance now offsets the NOL benefit (Q1 FY27 tax expense $16,500 on a $1.38m pre-tax loss), and the Hilti Complex rental income that sat in 'other income' ($619,500 in Q1 FY26) went with the building sale (Q1 FY27 'other' was a $103,700 expense); on Q1 FY27 opex run-rates (O&S $0.68m, commissions ~29% of PaperPie revenue, G&A $2.07m) and ~$4.2m of revenue at 58% gross margin, the pre-tax loss is about $(1.4)-(1.6)m, EPS around $(0.16)-(0.19) against $(0.15).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-09: net loss widened to $(1.40)m from $(1.08)m on the same tax and other-income swing and the stock fell 3.18%; 2026-05-19 (Q4 FY26 loss $(3.1)m with a $1.5m valuation allowance) fell 3.36%.
findings.why_not_priced: The retail base's narrative since the Hilti sale is 'debt-free, interest gone, costs cut $1.2m': if the market expected the loss to stay flat or widen, it would not need the company to say it, but no estimate exists and the 10-Q's tax and other-income mechanics are not in any wire summary. A print of $(0.17) beside a year-ago $(0.15) reads as a miss to a holder expecting the interest saving to show.
findings.independence: Year-ago opex, interest and tax lines from the Q2 FY26 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/31667/000118518525001415/educ10q083125.htm, 2025-10-09); the valuation-allowance mechanics from the Q4 FY26 release (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/298021/Educational-Development-Corporation-Announces-Fiscal-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-2026-Results, 2026-05-19). This is a derivation from documents, not a company statement about Q2.

findings.finding: Usborne, 33% of PaperPie revenue in Q1 FY27 (48% in the year-ago Q2), can terminate the distribution agreement on under 30 days' notice: the 10-Q states the company did not meet minimum purchase volumes and 'did not supply the letter of credit required under the Agreement', Usborne has refused a $1.0m FY22 volume rebate, and Usborne purchases were $0 in the quarter; the Q2 10-Q is the next place a termination notice or a further cut in Usborne share would appear.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has carried a Usborne termination; the same disclosure has sat in every 10-Q and the 10-K (filed 2026-05-19) without a notice, and those prints moved -0.7% to -3.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: The termination right is disclosed, so the risk is in the price to the extent anyone reads the note; what is not priced is the direction of the Usborne share and whether purchases resumed in Q2 with the revolver (which was obtained 'to support purchases of new titles'). A resumption would show as Usborne purchases above $0; a notice would be an 8-K-level event. Sized at the probability-weighted tail, not at the headline.
findings.independence: 10-K FY26 confirms minimums unmet in FY25 and FY26 and no notice received (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000031667/000118518526001927/educ10k022826.htm, 2026-05-19). Same company documents; no outside source on Usborne's intentions was found.

findings.finding: Publishing faces an inflated comp: the year-ago Q2 FY26 Publishing revenue of $889,900 was lifted by 'additional discounts offered to retail customers in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 to spur sales' (10-Q), and Publishing was already down 40% YoY in Q1 FY27 ($580,900 vs $1,046,100); a repeat of that rate puts Publishing near $0.55m, about $0.35m or 7.5% of total year-ago revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Publishing is ~15% of revenue; no print has visibly traded on it. Net of the rest: PaperPie (85%) would need to be flat YoY on 10% fewer partners for total revenue to reach $4.62m, which is the partner and new-title findings above, so this is sized at the segment's own weight only.
findings.why_not_priced: The discount-driven year-ago Publishing number is a footnote in a 10-Q nobody summarises; a reader comparing headline revenue to $4.6m would not know $0.1-0.2m of it was promotional.
findings.independence: Q1 FY27 segment table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/31667/000118518526002870/educ10q053126.htm, 2026-07-09) for the -40% run-rate.

findings.finding: Financing: the $2.0m Regent Bank revolver (Prime+2%, matures 2027-03-06, CEO personal guarantee) was undrawn at 31 May with cash at $1,662,500 (up from $1,118,400), operating cash flow +$564,300 on a $(1.40)m loss because inventory fell $1.5m to $36.2m; the CFO's stated goal is cash-flow positive over the next three quarters, so the Q2 cash line (up again, or a first draw) is the check on whether inventory liquidation still funds the loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-09 (cash up $0.5m, revolver undrawn) fell 3.18%; the stock has not paid for cash generation from inventory. Going-concern doubt was alleviated in the 10-K.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: the facility was obtained for new-title purchases, is undrawn, and the company has $36m of inventory against an $11m market cap to liquidate, so it is not distress; signed as a small positive to zero. A draw in Q2 would flip it. If the market treated the balance sheet as safe the stock would not trade at a third of inventory.
findings.independence: Regent 8-K of 2026-03-11 for the terms and purpose (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/31667/000118518526000844/educ8k031126.htm); CFO cash-flow goal from the call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15219109458093056, 2026-07-09).

findings.finding: Industry proxies point mildly both ways: Circana/PW reported children's as the only print category up in Q1 2026 while total print units fell 3.1%, and the DSA's 2025 report (via a secondary source) has US direct sellers down 3.7% and retail sales down 1.44%, so the product category is holding while the channel shrinks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; this name has never visibly traded on an industry series.
findings.why_not_priced: A proxy, not a company number; filed small. Children's demand being firm is the condition under which a stabilised salesforce converts to revenue.
findings.independence: Proxy. DSA figures via https://www.epixelmlmsoftware.com/industry-news/us-direct-selling-performance-2025 (secondary source, 2025 full year).

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Scholastic (quarter ended 31 Aug 2026, reported 2026-09-24) had revenue down 4% to $216.8m with Children's Book Publishing and Distribution among the declining lines, shares -12% after hours, but reaffirmed FY27 guidance and called trade momentum positive into Q2; a weak summer for the largest US children's publisher is a mild negative proxy for EDC's Publishing segment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; EDC has never traded on a Scholastic print.
findings.why_not_priced: A proxy; Scholastic's decline was driven by Education and lost rental income, not by trade demand, so the transmission to EDC is weak and sized accordingly.
findings.independence: Proxy; same period as EDC's quarter. Call summary at https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-scholastic-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-09-24/.

outside_window.finding: The Regent Bank $2.0m revolver matures 2027-03-06 and carries a CEO personal guarantee; a renewal or non-renewal is a 2027 event.

baseline_tension: Cuts mildly against nothing: there is no skew, the run-up is flat, and the only market statement is a reaction history that is 1 up in 7, which the negative lean agrees with; the partner stabilisation is the one thing that would argue the pattern breaks and it was already shown on 9 July and sold.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the partner-stabilisation finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8 because the same fact was disclosed on 9 July and the stock fell 3.2% that day; p_up left at 45.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): no consensus exists, the bar is the company's own year-ago 10-Q; all sizes were already capped small and the bar field says so; no size changed.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the revolver finding was already signed after asking what the money buys (undrawn, for titles, cash rising); unchanged at +0.2.
Rule 5 (proxies filed small): DSA/Circana and Scholastic proxies left at +0.2 / -0.2.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): the Publishing comp finding already states what PaperPie must do; unchanged at -0.3.
Rule 3 (caveats reach the number): the partner and net-loss findings are not contradictory (partners can stabilise while the loss does not narrow); both kept.
